title.rendered: Burn Ban Continues Despite Rain Forecast

content.rendered: (Undated) — While the current forecast is calling for a chance of rain this weekend, a burn ban remains in effect. Crawford County authorities remind the public that a countywide burn ban continues until further notice. Authorities say that at this time, no open burning is allowed with the exception of small contained fires for cooking purposes. The current forecast from the National Weather Service is calling for scattered showers Friday night through Sunday morning. However, authorities say “substantial rain” will be needed to lift the ban. Stay tuned to Classic Hits, WTYE, for the latest weather information.

title.rendered: Countywide Burn Ban Now in Effect Until Further Notice

content.rendered: (Undated) — Following an extended period of dry weather, a Burn Ban has been put in place. Crawford County Sheriff, Bill Rutan, in conjunction with local fire officials, has officially instituted a county-wide Burn Ban. Authorities say conditions in our area are currently “far too dry and we do not want issues in our county.” They say that at this time, no open burning is allowed with the exception of small contained fires for cooking purposes. The ban will remain in effect until further notice.

title.rendered: Slow Moving Front Forecast to Bring Needed Rain

content.rendered:
(Undated) — DTN Ag Meteorologist, John Baranick, is calling the current weather “a second burst of summer.”
Baranick says a very slow front continues to move into the area and should bring some much-needed rain over the weekend.
He says since the front is moving so slowly, we should have multiple days with shower chances. Saying rain should be possible through at least Monday. Rain is needed as Crawford County remains under a burn ban.
